Interpretation Notes

  • Map rows exercise the public ImtMap wrapper; set rows exercise the public ImtSet wrapper with value_bytes=0.
  • std::string map rows still allocate key and value character buffers per entry, so payload bytes can dominate jemalloc allocated memory.
  • PackedString rows use a smaller string object and packed block storage for block-tree cases, which should make block-level memory savings more visible.
  • Block structure tables only include block-tree backed rows because tree-backed rows do not expose zip-list block stats.
